scope: Persisted tenant-flow configuration and same-company authorization for coordinator actors in API and Cloud.

environment.database: Separate disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 databases for API and Cloud on localhost.
environment.fixtures: Synthetic coordinator accounts for tenant A and B plus two owned definitions each; all UAT-080 rows and users were removed after verification.
environment.restart: Both local services restarted against the same isolated database before readback.
environment.network: Local API/Cloud HTTP and PostgreSQL only; no customer call or CRM endpoint was invoked.

assertions_per_backend: Registration produced ordinary user accounts before isolated database preparation assigned coordinator role and tenant scope.
Tenant A and B coordinators each created company-owned flow definitions while submitting forged company IDs; the current database company prevailed.
Definition reads ignored a forged foreign company query and returned only the coordinator's company definitions.
Tenant A updated and archived its own definition; a foreign-definition update returned no record.
Coordinators created draft versions under their own definitions; a foreign-parent version create returned 400; approval succeeded and later edits were rejected.
Tenant A upserted an enablement permission, disabled it while retaining the same row, and received 400 for a foreign-definition permission.
Tenant A upserted an intent mapping, replaced its allowed-flow IDs on update, and received 400 for a foreign-definition mapping.
After API/Cloud restart, coordinator-scoped reads returned the archived definition, approved version, disabled retained permission and replacement mapping while excluding Tenant B rows.
Database verification found zero UAT-080 accounts, definitions, versions, permissions or mappings after cleanup.
limitations: This closes the four coordinator/API matrix rows only; Web, other-role and superadmin rows remain open.
No live flow execution or customer-selected call/CRM integration was tested.
